summary: toSpliced creates a new array with a range removed or replaced.
documentation: toSpliced creates a new array with a range removed or replaced. It leaves its receiver unchanged and returns the whole revised array, unlike splice, which mutates and returns removed items.
inputs: A start position, deletion count and replacement items.
returns: A new array containing the revised sequence.
caution: This requires a modern engine. A copy is shallow; nested objects are still shared references.
scenarios: Preview a route adjustment before saving its original itinerary.
Insert new shift slots into a proposed schedule.
Replace several cart rows in an immutable editing state.
title: Preview a schedule edit
problem: Input has items, start, deleteCount and insertions arrays/integers. start is between 0 and items.length; deleteCount is nonnegative. Return {original: unchangedItems, updated: revisedItems}, removing up to deleteCount items at start and inserting every element from insertions there.
goal: Use Array.toSpliced() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Spread insertions into toSpliced and retain the original array.
